detailed_rationale:
CG Power delivered a genuinely strong FY26: consolidated revenue of Rs 12,418cr (+25% YoY) and consolidated PAT of roughly Rs 1,200-1,232cr (+23-27% YoY depending on the exceptional-items cut used), with Q4 FY26 alone printing Rs 3,441.8cr revenue (+25%) and Rs 365.5cr PAT (+33%). The order book, the real tell for a capital-goods name, hit a record consolidated Rs 17,107cr (+61% YoY) - but the split matters: Power Systems (transformers, reactors, switchgear) carries Rs 12,644cr of that (80% of the book, order inflow +69% YoY), while Industrial Systems (motors, generators) trails with the remainder. Margins are equally lopsided and moving in opposite directions: Power Systems ran a 22% EBIT margin in FY26, while Industrial Systems actually contracted 230bps YoY to 9.3% (from 11.6%) on commodity cost pressure and competitive/mix pressure in railways, despite banking cumulative 17.5% price hikes in motors during the year. So the headline 'record' year conceals a two-speed business: a high-margin Power Systems franchise riding India's ~Rs 9.2 lakh crore planned transmission capex through 2032 plus a new, higher-margin export vein (a Rs 900cr US hyperscale-data-centre transformer order in January 2026), subsidizing a larger, structurally lower-margin motors business that is losing pricing power. Balance sheet quality is not in question - debt/equity ~0.01, interest coverage ~65x, ROE ~35%, ROCE ~33% (quant context, corroborated by the scale of FY26 profit growth on a near-debt-free base) - under credible Murugappa-group governance since the 2020 turnaround from the pre-Murugappa (Avantha-era) fraud period.

The CG Semi OSAT venture (JV with Renesas ~6.8% and Stars Microelectronics ~0.9%, CG holding ~92.3%) reached a real execution milestone: the Rs 7,600cr G1 facility at Sanand began commercial production on 4 July 2026 (PM-inaugurated), already exporting packaged chips to Malaysia, with a second G2 line targeted by end-CY2026. CG's own equity commitment is capped near $205mn (~Rs 1,700cr), manageable against its net-cash balance sheet and >Rs 1,200cr annual PAT, so this is not a solvency risk - but it is a genuine near-term earnings drag: management flagged a Rs 38cr (~110bps) negative margin impact from the semiconductor vertical in Q4 FY26 alone, and global OSAT economics are thin and volatile until scale and customer diversification (currently anchored to Renesas) are proven over multiple years. Separately, Axiro Semiconductor (fabless RF/chip design, a $36mn Bengaluru design centre, plus a stake in AI-chip startup EdgeCortix) is a smaller, earlier-stage option reportedly contributing ~Rs 400cr of FY26 revenue with limited independent profitability disclosure. Both should be treated as legitimate long-dated options on India's semiconductor build-out, not as proven earnings drivers, and they add capital-allocation and execution risk on top of a core business that does not need it at this valuation.

This is where the call turns. CG Power trades at roughly 108-120x trailing consolidated earnings (market cap ~Rs 1.4 lakh cr; sources cluster between 108x on a TTM cut and 115-120x on the FY26 print) - a premium even to expensive listed peers (ABB India ~93x, Siemens India ~67-94x) and near all-time-high multiples after a ~48-56% six-month rally. Even the bulls concede growth is largely priced in: Nomura's own model assumes a punchy 31% EPS CAGR FY26-29 and still only derives a Rs 1,100 target, ~17-19% above CMP (~Rs 905-925) - the sell-side's best-case growth scenario buys a mid-teens return, not a re-rating. Ambit, by contrast, carries a Sell at Rs 650 (~30% downside), built on a specific, checkable structural point: India's own National Electricity Plan projects over 30% lower high-voltage transmission capacity additions in FY27-32 versus FY22-27 - a multi-year deceleration risk squarely in the segment (Power Systems) supplying 80% of CG's order book and virtually all of its margin upside. A reverse-DCF sanity check confirms the asymmetry: justifying the current multiple with a still-generous 25x exit multiple in five years requires a sustained ~45-50% EPS CAGR - well above even Nomura's 31% bull case and roughly double management's own mid-20s% FY27 revenue guidance. The business is excellent; the price already assumes it stays excellent indefinitely, with no room for the margin cracks already visible in Industrial Systems or the capex-cycle deceleration risk flagged by the government's own planning document.
recommendation_rationale: Sell, not Hold, because the valuation gap here is not a marginal stretch - it is priced meaningfully past even the sell-side's own bull case (Nomura's 31% EPS CAGR FY26-29 supports only ~17-19% further upside), while the largest and highest-margin segment (Power Systems, 80% of the order book) faces a credible, quantified structural deceleration argument from a specific bear case (Ambit, Rs 650 target, ~30% downside, grounded in the National Electricity Plan's own FY27-32 transmission-capex trajectory). Layer on visible margin erosion already showing in the other core segment (Industrial Systems, -230bps YoY) and an unprofitable, capital- and attention-absorbing OSAT/semiconductor bolt-on, and the risk-reward skews to the downside despite genuinely excellent operating performance and balance-sheet quality. This is a sell-the-price, not sell-the-business, call.
summary: CG Power had an excellent FY26 - revenue and profit both grew strongly and the order book hit a record high - and the balance sheet remains debt-free with very high returns on capital. But the market has already priced in years of continued strong growth: the stock trades near its most expensive level ever, well above global peers such as ABB and Siemens India, and even optimistic broker forecasts (assuming roughly 30% earnings growth for three more years) only justify a modest further gain from here, while at least one major broker sees roughly 30% downside if India's transmission-equipment investment cycle slows after FY27 as currently planned. Margins in the company's motors business have also weakened this year, and a new chip-manufacturing venture is still a small drag on quarterly profit while it scales up. We are not questioning CG Power's business quality - we are flagging that the price leaves very little room for anything to go wrong.
positive_para: FY26 was a genuinely strong year: consolidated revenue grew 25% to Rs 12,418cr and PAT grew over 20%, with Q4 alone posting 25% revenue growth and 33% PAT growth. The order book hit a record Rs 17,107cr, up 61% YoY, with Power Systems (transformers/switchgear) inflows up 69% YoY on the back of India's ~Rs 9.2 lakh crore planned transmission capex through 2032, plus a new, higher-margin export vein in hyperscale-data-centre transformers (a Rs 900cr US order in January 2026). The balance sheet is close to debt-free (D/E ~0.01) with ~65x interest coverage and ~35% ROE, under credible post-turnaround Murugappa governance. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in the mid-20s% with EBITDA margin expanding to 14-15%, and capacity additions (transformer capacity nearly doubling to 110,000 MVA by end-CY2026; a Rs 748cr switchgear greenfield expansion) are already funded and underway. The CG Semi OSAT venture also hit a real milestone - commercial production started in July 2026, ahead of many domestic semiconductor peers - giving the company a genuine, first-mover option on India's chip-packaging build-out.
negative_para: The valuation has run far ahead of even generous growth assumptions. At ~108-120x trailing earnings and a market cap near Rs 1.4 lakh cr, CG Power trades above already-rich peers (ABB India ~93x, Siemens ~67-94x) near all-time-high multiples after a ~48-56% six-month rally. Nomura's own bull case (31% EPS CAGR FY26-29) supports only a Rs 1,100 target - ~17-19% upside from CMP - while Ambit's Sell case (Rs 650, ~30% downside) rests on a specific, checkable structural point: the National Electricity Plan itself projects over 30% lower high-voltage transmission capacity additions in FY27-32 versus FY22-27, directly threatening the segment (Power Systems) that supplies 80% of CG's order book and virtually all of its margin expansion. Underneath the headline growth, Industrial Systems (the larger revenue segment) already shows cracks: EBIT margin fell 230bps YoY to 9.3% on commodity cost pressure and competitive intensity in railways, even after 17.5% cumulative motor price hikes - a sign not every part of this 'record' year is clean execution. The semiconductor bets (CG Semi OSAT, Axiro/EdgeCortix) are real but unproven: OSAT alone dragged Q4 margins by ~110bps, is customer-concentrated (anchored on Renesas), and sits in a global segment known for thin, volatile economics until scale is proven over multiple years - a multi-year cash and management-attention commitment layered onto an already fully-priced core business.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~108-120x trailing consolidated earnings, the market is pricing CG Power for a sustained ~45-50% EPS CAGR over the next five years if it is to de-rate to a still-generous 25x exit multiple - almost double the 31% EPS CAGR (FY26-29) that Nomura's own bull case models, and well above management's own mid-20s% FY27 revenue guidance. Put differently: even the sell-side's optimistic scenario supports only ~17-19% further re-rating (Nomura Rs 1,100 target vs CMP ~Rs 905-925), while a credible bear case grounded in the government's own National Electricity Plan (>30% lower HV transmission capacity adds FY27-32 vs FY22-27) supports ~30% downside (Ambit Rs 650). The multiple has effectively no margin of safety left; it is priced for perfection in a cyclical, capex-dependent business that has just shown its first cracks (Industrial Systems margin compression) in an otherwise clean year. Judgment: rich, not fair, not cheap.
